title: ONLY THREE DAYS LEFT!
text: Thursday | 1st December 2005 ONLY THREE DAYS LEFT! Nuff respect due. Last night, your boy Sabzi entered the third installment of the Big Tunes beat battle hosted by Vitamin D. With Maseo, ?uestLove and the town's biggest producers in the house, and against a solid lineup including Bean One and Smoke, our resident beatsmith dropped heater after heater and came home with the crown. Big up! *** BallerStatus.net says the Blue Scholars LP is a "pretty solid effort." Meanwhile, Oregon's The Daily Vanguard spits hot fiyah at us, claiming "You don't need a message to make great music" and that "classic hip-hop albums don't have big social messages." Guess It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back and By All Means Necessary aren't classics.

title: THE STRANGER & SEATTLE WEEKLY
text: Wednesday | 30th November 2005 THE STRANGER & SEATTLE WEEKLY The Long March EP album release party is listed in this week's The Stanger Suggests , and the EP was reviewed as one of Charles Mudede's top Seattle hip-hop albums of 2005 (which also includes the Common Market album) in last week's The Stranger issue. Read the article here: Seattle Blows Up with Local Hiphop . *** This week's Seattle Weekly music section features Blue Scholars, son! Here's a snippet: So far, Blue Scholars--the Seattle hip-hop duo of 23-year-old DJ Sabzi and MC Geologic, 25--have avoided that hoariest of pop-music cliches by not writing bitchy songs about The Road. But maybe they're due. The first time I interviewed them for this piece, they had just returned from a weeklong road trip; the group drove me in their touring van to the Moonlight Cafe in the International District for a convivial, entertaining lunch. Two days later, they would get in it again and travel down the coast for some more shows--right around the time I discovered that the microphone I'd conducted the interview with had been dead the entire time. Read the rest of the article here: Proletariat Blues

title: Recovered LiveJournal entry
text: Friday | 11th November 2005 Peace to Oakland: always been a fan of The Coup @ The Casbah, San Diego Warm militant greetings, online fam. It's day 7 on the road (halfway through the damn thing), and last we checked Iraq is still under foreign occupation and it now takes three instead of two $20 bills to fill a full tank of gas for a Honda Odyssey. Euguene, Portland, San Diego and LA... all a blur right now. We'll let it marinate and drop an update when we get back. Thanks to the folks who let us crash at their spot, came out to a show, or copped some merch. Peace to our fam we didn't get to see before rolling out. Yall have made some Northwesterners feel right at home, and not just because it's rained in every city we've been thus far.

title: MEDIA UPDATES
text: Wednesday | 28th September 2005 MEDIA UPDATES Geo and Sabzi are featured in the latest and final issue of Tablet Magazine (RIP) . Entertainment World did a feature on Blue Scholars in their Indie section, with an interview with Geo. Lastly, for those of yall who can read and speak Norwegian, we were interviewed and featured in the July issue of Putsj . --- MISC 1. We will be hitting up cities on both coasts in November. More details to come, very soon. 2. The Long March EP will be released in early December, beginning with a release party at Chop Suey. 3. Sabzi and RA Scion have completed a collaboration album under the moniker Common Market , and will be rocking with Abyssinian Creole, DJ B-Mello and KRS-One (!!) at their album release party on October 24 at Chop Suey (all-ages, yall), followed by a mini-tour throughout the Northwest with the Blastmaster. 4. One more thing, for those of you fueling false rumors that Blue Scholars is "breaking up" or leaving Seattle, please chiggity check yourselves before you wriggity wreck yourselves. You know who you are (and we know who some of you are, too). Quit that.
